subject: MSA + Order Form — proposed narrow 3P indemnity roadmap and review timeline
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@stargenix.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: legal-ops@stargenix.ai, Elise Chen <elise.chen@stargenix.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline — limiting Redwood exposure on 3rd-party IP claims

Team — thanks for sending the draft. Attached is our annotated MSA (PDF) and a short note from procurement highlighting the key asks. High level: Stargenix cannot accept an open-ended indemnity for third-party IP claims related to model outputs. We want a pragmatic middle ground so the deal can close this quarter.

Our suggested path:
- Limit customer-triggered indemnity to proven direct copying of customer-supplied content (i.e., not general model hallucination).
- Add a narrow carveout where customer·provided training datasets that contain third‑party content remain the customer's responsibility.
- Keep defense control with Redwood, but require an evidence-first notice window and a mutual cooperation clause.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (1) tie indemnity triggers to a demonstrated infringement event, (2) accept an order-form cap on indemnity tied to one year of fees, and (3) add an evidence-handoff SLA so we can satisfy our compliance team?

Attached: Stargenix-MSA-redline-2028-07-30.pdf

We aim to get to a signed order form by Aug 14. Please advise timeline and a single point of contact for legal redlines.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Procurement, Stargenix AI

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@stargenix.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline — limiting Redwood exposure on 3rd-party IP claims

Sanjay — thanks, and appreciated the clear asks. Quick reply with our proposed roadmap so legal/procurement can align:

1) Trigger definition: we can accept narrowing the trigger to "alleged infringement arising from Customer-supplied content or Customer-directed training artifacts". For model-generated outputs we propose a rebuttable presumption that Redwood is not liable unless Customer furnishes evidence tying the output to specific third-party content in Customer inputs.

2) Cap: we are open to an Order Form–level cap equal to 1x annual committed fees for the product that produced the alleged output (we'll flag this to Finance).

3) Evidence SLA & cooperation: agree to a 10-business-day preliminary evidence window after notice where Customer produces the alleged infringing material, logs, and prompt history; Redwood will preserve relevant runtime logs and KV cache snapshots for 30 days pending a litigation hold.

Next steps: Kimberly — can you draft redline language that implements the trigger + rebuttable presumption + the 10-business-day evidence window? Aditya — please confirm whether the 1x fees cap is ok operationally. I propose a short internal sync tomorrow at 10:30 to finalize language, then we share a single redline back to Stargenix.

Attachments: Redwood-proposed-indemnity-snippets-v1.docx

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@stargenix.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2028 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline — narrow trigger + evidence SLA — draft language attached

On Tue, Jul 30, 2028 at 11:05 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus outlines a solid path. I ran a quick pass on redlines and attached a draft (see docx). Key elements I added:

- Narrow trigger clause: "Customer Indemnity Trigger: Customer shall indemnify Redwood for third‑party claims to the extent such claims arise solely from (i) Customer-supplied training data or (ii) Customer-provided content that is demonstrably identical to the infringing material cited by the third party."
- Rebuttable presumption: language clarifying that for claims alleging model output infringement, Customer must provide a reasonably specific exemplar and related prompt history before liability attaches.
- Defense control & cooperation: Redwood retains defense control for speed but with a mandatory status update cadence (every 10 business days) and a right for Customer to propose counsel if Redwood declines to defend.
- Cap: recommended order-form cap = 1x annual fees for the impacted product; propose carveouts for willful misconduct.

Procurement note: If Stargenix accepts the evidence SLA, we will include an evidence checklist in the order form appendix (logs, prompt export, dataset slice). That appendix will be non-public and subject to redaction rules.

Please review the attached and call out anything that materially changes our exposure. I think this keeps the commercial deal intact while protecting the platform.

Attachments: Redwood-proposed-indemnity-snippets-v1.docx

—Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@stargenix.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Elise Chen <elise.chen@stargenix.ai>, legal-ops@stargenix.ai
Date: Wed, 31 Jul 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline — proposed narrow 3P indemnity roadmap and review timeline

Marcus / Kimberly — appreciate the quick turnaround and the concrete language. The narrow trigger + rebuttable presumption is acceptable in principle. Procurement is aligned on the 1x annual-fees cap with the standard willful-misconduct carveout. Legal Ops asked for two small edits:

1) Shorten the evidence window to 7 business days (we have a time-sensitive compliance audit).
2) Add an explicit mutual non-waiver sentence so neither party's cooperation during triage is treated as an admission.

If Redwood can accept those two items we are ready to move to redline-to-sign: please send the clean redline and a DocuSign link. Target: sign by Aug 10.

On Wed, Jul 30, 2028 at 03:22 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> (quoted for context)

Thanks — Sanjay. I'll make the 7-business-day change and add the non-waiver sentence; Marcus / Aditya — confirm final cap language and I'll circulate the single redline.

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Procurement, Stargenix AI
